newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks finish in red on Yeltsin rumours.
newsitem.headline: French stocks finish in red on Yeltsin rumours.

text.p: French shares finished in the red on Wednesday after rumours about Russian President Boris Yeltsin's health pulled Wall Street sharply lower. Russia later denied the rumours and said Yelstin was in satisfactory condition.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 14.83 points or 0.69 percent at 2,146.71 after spending much of the day fluctuating in a narrow range between negative and positive territory. The CAC-40 futures contract settled at 2,148.0, down from Monday's close of 2,168.0.

Anglo-French channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel was 10.2 percent down at 7.50 francs after falling as low as 6.95 francs earlier in the day on investor disappointment over debt relief deal with creditor banks.
Analysts said the share was for speculators only and added that prospects for profits and dividends are too intangible to put a value on the share with any degree of certainty.
"Basically the share's worth nothing any longer. Speculators buy and sell and play with it, it keeps the market occupied," said one analyst at a Paris brokerage.
